lightbulb Strategy Insight

The Best First Move is a Corner

While the Center is the most defensive start, playing a Corner is the aggressive "Pro Move." It forces your opponent into a specific response (the center) to avoid losing immediately.

analytics Move Analysis

The Corner Start Win Rate: ~91%*

The most aggressive opening. Mathematically, if you start in a corner, your opponent MUST play the center. If they play anywhere else (edge or corner), you can force a win 100% of the time.

The Center Start Safe & Solid

The classic defensive move. It participates in 4 possible winning lines. However, opponents have 4 "safe" responses (any corner), making it harder to trap them than the corner start.

The Edge Start Weakest

Generally considered the weakest opening. It only contributes to 2 winning lines and gives the opponent many ways to force a draw or even win if you aren't careful.

* Win rate against a random/novice player who doesn't know the perfect defense.

Why does the Corner Win?

In Tic-Tac-Toe, a "fork" is when you create two winning lines simultaneously. Starting in the Corner gives you the most opportunities to create these forks if your opponent slips up and doesn't take the center. Starting in the Center is safer, but harder to create forks from because the opponent's only job is to play a corner.
